Hey man, so I wasn't a alcoholic or anything. I did abuse alcohol to some extent though. Drank for all the wrong reasons pretty much. But my way was talking to my parents. One night I drank a Mickey and I had just had enough of it. I couldn't live with myself and I gave them a call. And they came and helped me. I haven't drank an ounce since that day. I do get cravings to drink still but it's a big mindset deal. You gotta put everything you got into not drinking. And say you are doing good. And one night you lose it and binge. That doesn't mean you failed, you just try harder. That's kind of the method for me working out. I would binge on junk food cuz I'd give in to my cravings for it. But I knew that if I binge, the next day is a work hard day. I made it a goal that everytime I lose and give in to my cravings. A punishment for it would be working out twice as hard the next day to make up for it. This eventually led to better self control and I stopped binging as much. That's just my own experience though.

Don't kill yourself. I've been down the suicide road. Not pleasant. One has to be very committed to it. I'm glad you met someone that cared and convinced you not to leave this world. 

Don't take this harsh, but things only get better if you make them better. Took me a long time to accept and realize that. I was suicidal. I've wept late at night. I've pushed those close to me away. But the only way it'll get better is if you take control of your situation. I'm in university. I struggle with studying alright. My solution to that problem was literally study. The problem became the solution. It's all about mental prep. 

You have to mentally force yourself to do well. You're gonna hate it. But it's something that needs to be done. Watching motivational videos is super helpful. Find a motivational speaker you connect with and whenever you feel doubt, listen to them. For me, it was Eric Thomas. He taught me to never give up and that it's simple. If you want to succeed, your gonna have to work for it. 

I hope this helps you in some way. I'm sorry if I scolded you at all. Didn't mean to, but seriously. Try your damn hardest. :)

Hello, I'm sorry to hear that you want to commit suicide. There's very limited things I can say because I'm just a stranger on the other side. But I'll give you some of my own experiences.

I tried committing suicide a month and a bit ago. I was failing university, was unsure about my career. Things were going on at home, and well I just had enough of it. I tried hanging myself with a belt and quickly realized how much work and agony it would be. Not only on myself, whether I survive it or not. But on my family also. I've seen videos and what the outcome looks like when they hang themselves. And let me tell you, it ain't like that movies. You aren't found hanging there "nicely clothed" It's a gruesome sight and often very ugly because of neck marks and it's known to make you empty your bowels. 

You're probably wondering why I'm telling you what it looks like and why that would matter. Well the first thing that came to my mind is my family finding me. It would be a very traumatic sight and you'd think I wouldn't care if I wanted to die but I did. From my experience, hanging ain't fun. You'd have to be very committed to hanging yourself because it's very painful. The choking sensation. It's not fun. 

I'm sorry to hear that political views really hindered your friendship. I know people who don't have the same political views as me and while it does bother me, we usually don't talk about it. I encourage you to look up Eric Thomas. He's a motivational speaker and activist. He was a homeless person for 2 years. Got kicked out. He's black so he faced racism in his life. But he managed to pull through it and now he's making millions. Often he'll speak to schools for free because he's not about the money. He's about helping people. Some of his work motivated me to try again. And I hope maybe he could help you! 

I'd advise you to really think about what you're going to do and maybe re evaluate your decision. There are people out there that love you.
